# Difficult Workplace Conversations

## 1. Classify before drafting

Settle four things first: the user's role and power relative to each person; the outcome they want; the stakes and urgency; and whether a formal process (HR, investigation, union, legal) already applies. Ask only for the one fact that changes the route; draft the rest with bracketed placeholders.

| Situation | Go to | Load |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Threats, harassment, discrimination, retaliation, safety | Section 7 first | nothing |
| Compensation, promotion, title, or workload terms | Section 3 | preparation-template.md only for a written worksheet |
| Delivering a decision the person will not want | Section 4 | delivery-scripts.md only to rehearse reactions |
| A conflict the user is in: public criticism, a blowup, disputed facts | Section 5 | delivery-scripts.md only to rehearse reactions |
| Raising a sensitive personal matter (health, family) | delivery-scripts.md sensitive-matter line (impact on work plus the adjustment needed; the diagnosis is optional); Section 7 if it involves harassment | delivery-scripts.md |
| A dispute between other people | Section 6 gate | facilitation.md only after the gate passes |
| User may lose composure, or already did | Section 2 | emotional-regulation.md only if they ask for a technique |
| Feedback on one behavior, recognition, a reply to vague criticism, a scope or deadline reset, a recap | the feedback-mastery skill | nothing from this skill |

Tie-break: if a single behavior is the topic but the relationship has already broken down (a blowup, a failed earlier attempt, disputed facts), use Section 5; otherwise hand off to feedback-mastery.

## 2. Readiness

Before scheduling, ask the user: can you state the other person's likely account in one sentence they would agree with, and listen for two minutes without rebutting? If not, wait: draft the message but do not send it, and fix a specific reconvening time ("Thursday 10:00"), not "when things calm down". An open-ended pause reads as avoidance and the issue resurfaces worse. If the time is fixed by someone else or by a decision timeline (a decision delivery already scheduled, a manager-booked 1:1), do not postpone: shorten the goal to the one point that must be made, prepare the opening and one buying-time line ([phrase-bank.md](references/phrase-bank.md)), and book the deeper conversation for a dated slot.

Readiness never delays urgent matters. Safety goes to Section 7 now; so do harassment, discrimination, retaliation and formal proceedings, at once, and the raise-it-now exception below covers only operational incidents that are none of these. An urgent operational issue (a broken release, a customer at risk) is raised now with the decision owner, facts only; the relationship conversation waits for a dated slot.

Repair after the user got defensive: one sentence owning the specific behavior ("I cut you off and argued instead of listening"), no explanation of why, then a question that returns to the substance. An explanation attached to an apology is heard as an excuse.

Read [phrase-bank.md](references/phrase-bank.md) only when the user needs lines to buy time in the room or to say they are triggered. Read [preparation-template.md](references/preparation-template.md) only when their goals, the time and place, or a named preparation habit (over-preparing, winging it, preparing to attack or to avoid) needs work. For a short readiness question, answer from this file and load neither.

When the conversation must happen before a weekend, leave, or a long absence, arrange named support (an HR contact, EAP details, a person to talk to) and book the follow-up date in the same conversation; otherwise the person is left alone with it until the return.

## 3. Negotiation

1. **Make the concrete ask.** Opening = purpose + evidence + specific ask + openness to alternatives. "I'd like to discuss my compensation. Since my last adjustment I led the payments launch and have two strong review cycles. I'm asking for an increase to [figure] by [cycle/date]. If that isn't possible, I'd like to understand what would get there." State the figure, then stop talking; revising it before they answer negotiates against yourself.
2. **Classify each objection before answering it:**

| They say | Type | Respond |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "You're not operating at the next level yet" | evidence | Ask which criterion and which example would change their view; agree what to show by when. |
| "Budget is frozen until Q3" | budget | Do not re-argue merit. Ask what is tradable now (title, scope, bonus, training, a written commitment with an amount range) and for a decision date when budget reopens. |
| "Raises only happen in the review cycle" | process | Ask when the cycle's inputs are fixed; calibration usually closes weeks before the review meeting, so asking at the meeting is too late. Ask to be put forward in that input. |
| "It's not my call" | authority | Ask who decides, whether they will advocate, what they need from the user to do it, and when they will report back. |

3. **Separate tradable from fixed terms.** Fixed: what policy sets (salary band, cycle dates). Tradable: timing, title, scope, bonus, review date, support. Asking for the band is legitimate and changes the next ask.
4. **Close with decision owner, criteria, and a dated checkpoint or explicit fallback:** "So [decider] will decide on [criteria] by [date]; if it's a no, we'll [fallback]." Then send the written summary (Section 8).

## 4. Delivering a decision

1. **Confirm the decision and reason with its actual owner** before the meeting. For layoffs, employment-status changes and other formal personnel decisions, deliver only HR's or the authorized owner's approved wording; improvised reasons create legal exposure and contradict the record. With no approved wording yet, do not deliver: get it agreed in writing first. For ordinary operational bad news (a cancelled project), verifying with the decision owner is enough; do not require HR, founder or legal sign-off. Offer only flexibility the owner has confirmed.
2. **State the decision in the first two sentences.** Warm-up small talk before bad news reads as cruel in hindsight, and a feedback sandwich buries it.
3. **Name what the person can still influence** (timing, references, how it is announced). Do not debate the decision; arguing it reopens it.
4. **Hand over written logistics and book the follow-up** (Section 8 summary, with the logistics line).

## 5. A conflict the user is in

Sort the user's account into three columns: observed facts (dated, checkable), disputed points, and interpretations (motive, intent). Open with the situation, the observable behavior, its impact, and an open question that invites their account: "In Monday's planning meeting, the release date changed after QA had signed off. That left the team without a test window. What drove the change, and how should we handle date changes from here?" For each disputed point, name what would settle it (ticket history, calendar, chat log) instead of arguing it; if it stays disputed, agree on the impact and the next step anyway, and record it as disputed.

Read [phrase-bank.md](references/phrase-bank.md) when the user needs an opening for another topic, a way to acknowledge without conceding, to redirect to facts or return to their point, to reframe a blaming sentence, or a line for a defensive person or an impasse.

## 6. Disputes between others: the joint-meeting gate

Gather each account separately first. Hold a joint meeting only if all hold:

- **Authority:** the user manages both parties or is an agreed facilitator, with no stake in which side wins.
- **Consent:** both parties agreed to meet after their separate conversations.
- **Suitability:** no allegation of harassment, discrimination, threats, or retaliation; no formal investigation underway; no direct reporting line between the two parties.

If any fails, do not script a joint meeting. Route instead: separate conversations, the parties' own lead or manager, HR, or a trusted facilitator both accept. A joint session after an allegation pressures the reporting person and can compromise an investigation; one without consent is an ambush. When the gate passes, load [facilitation.md](references/facilitation.md) for the session plan.

## 7. Escalation and boundaries

- Imminent danger: immediate safety first; never require a direct confrontation. Use local emergency or security support, or the organization's urgent safety channel.
- Harassment, discrimination, retaliation, policy violations, formal performance proceedings: default to HR. If HR or the user's normal manager is implicated, use the ethics hotline or a skip-level manager. Add the union representative when the user is covered.
- If those channels are absent or all implicated (e.g. a founder harasses in a small firm with no HR): do not require confrontation or mediation. Preserve records securely, identify independent confidential support (union representative, external worker-support organization, qualified local adviser), and help the user choose a reporting route they judge safe. Pointing to outside support is not legal advice.
- Preserve dates, observable conduct, witnesses, and relevant communications; mark direct observation apart from hearsay. Keep records secure and need-to-know.
- Never use informal coaching to replace a required process.

## 8. Follow up

Send a short factual summary within one working day; unwritten commitments reopen and spoken bad news is not retained.

```text
Summary of [date] conversation with [name]
Agreed: [action] / [owner] / [date]
Disputed: [point], to be settled by [record or person]
Logistics handed over: [dates, contacts, next steps]   (decisions only)
Next checkpoint: [date]; if not met: [fallback or escalation]
```

Read [closing-and-followup.md](references/closing-and-followup.md) for the spoken read-back before leaving the room, a cover note around the summary, the check-in agenda, or what to say when no agreement was reached.

## Gotchas

- **Assume any written summary may be read in a formal HR or legal process.** Write facts, agreements, and dates only; no speculation about health, motive, or character; share need-to-know.
- **Never present a disputed recollection as established fact.** The other person stops engaging with the substance and contests the record instead.
- **Never promise absolute confidentiality.** Safety, harassment, and legal duties can override it, and a broken promise costs more trust than an honest "I may have to escalate this".
- **Never accept "let's revisit later" without a date.** It is a soft no that resets the clock each time.
- **Never cite an outside offer or ultimatum the user will not act on.** If it is called, the user loses credibility and the relationship.
- **Never put the topic in a calendar invite title** ("Role discussion", "Performance concern"). Shared calendars expose it to others, and the person spends the hours before the meeting dreading it or asking around.
- **Never advise secretly recording the conversation.** Consent rules differ by jurisdiction and employer policy, and a covert recording can breach policy and weaken the user's standing in the formal process it was meant to support. Write a dated note of what was said right after instead, and for Section 7 matters keep records as that section says.

## Conditional references

Load only the file the route needs; for a short request, answer from this file alone.

- [preparation-template.md](references/preparation-template.md): only when the user asks for a written worksheet (a 10-minute quick prep or the full one), or when goals, time and place, or preparation habits need work.
- [phrase-bank.md](references/phrase-bank.md): only for wording a moment in the conversation (openings for other topics, acknowledging without conceding, buying time, returning to the point, reframes, an impasse).
- [closing-and-followup.md](references/closing-and-followup.md): only when closing the conversation, when no agreement came, or for a follow-up note or check-in agenda.
- [delivery-scripts.md](references/delivery-scripts.md): only to rehearse specific reactions (denial, deflection, attack, shutdown, distress, reactions to a decision), or to word a sensitive personal disclosure or an escalation to a manager.
- [emotional-regulation.md](references/emotional-regulation.md): only when the user asks how to stay composed (feeling-to-first-move table, one technique, night-before steps, reframes, pre-conversation ritual). Do NOT load it for negotiation or bad-news delivery.
- [facilitation.md](references/facilitation.md): only after the Section 6 gate passes.
